survivalkit.picker.title: Add
survivalkit.picker.footer: %s results · click to add · Esc closes
survivalkit.setting.common.enabled.toolt: Whether the module is on; saved with the profile.
survivalkit.setting.common.key.tooltip: The key that turns this module on and off.
survivalkit.module.autoeat.desc: Eats for you when hunger drops below your threshold, and leaves the hotbar as it found it.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.threshold_mo: Fixed eats once hunger falls below the hunger threshold. Automatic waits until the bar has room for all of what the chosen food gives, so not a point of it is wasted: steak (8) at 12, bread (5) at 15.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.threshold.to: Starts eating once hunger falls below this. 20 is a full bar.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.eat_early_wh: While health is below the value set here, eat whenever the hunger bar is not full instead of waiting for hunger, so natural healing never stops. Ordinary food only: golden apples belong to the golden apple rule, which goes first when its own threshold is crossed.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.early_eating: Eats without waiting for hunger while health is below this. 20 is full health.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.priority.too: Food to eat first, the most wanted at the top. Anything on this list always beats anything that is not.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.blocked.tool: Food that is never eaten. The harmful ones and chorus fruit ship blocked; take any of them off.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.fallback.too: If none of the food on the preferred list is in the inventory, which of the rest to eat; harmful food always comes last.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.golden_apple: Eat a golden apple when health runs low, whatever hunger says. Golden apples are never picked for hunger on their own; only this rule or the preference order spends them.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.enchanted_go: Let the health rule spend enchanted golden apples too. Off means plain ones only.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.health_thres: Reaches for a golden apple once health falls below this. 20 is full health.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.scope.toolti: Where food may be found. With the whole inventory, food from the backpack is swapped into the held slot and put back when the meal is over.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.return_to_sl: Go back to the hotbar slot that was selected before the meal.
Which hand the food is eaten from. With the off hand, the food is borrowed into it for the length of the meal and the sword or blocks in the main hand are never disturbed; whatever the off hand held comes back afterwards.
survivalkit.setting.autoeat.keep_offhand: With a totem of undying in the off hand, eat in the main hand that time and leave the totem where it is.
survivalkit.module.autototem.desc: Keeps a totem of undying in your off hand, and puts the next one there when it is spent.
survivalkit.setting.autototem.scope.tool: Where totems may be found. With the whole inventory, one from the backpack is used too.
survivalkit.setting.autototem.mode.toolt: When the totem is kept in the off hand. Always gives that hand over to the totem for good; the health threshold only borrows it once health runs low.
survivalkit.setting.autototem.health_thr: The totem goes into the off hand once health falls below this. 20 is full health.
survivalkit.setting.autototem.restore_of: Put back whatever was in the off hand once health is above the threshold again. Off means the totem stays.
survivalkit.setting.autototem.fallback.t: Items to put in the off hand once no totem is left, in order: the first one found in the inventory goes in. Left empty, the hand stays empty. A totem takes the item's place as soon as one turns up.
survivalkit.setting.autototem.warn_when_: Put one line in chat when a totem is wanted and none is left. A new totem arms the warning again.
survivalkit.autototem.out_of_totems: Out of totems — the off hand has none.
survivalkit.module.autoweapon.desc: With a weapon in hand, takes out the best one for whatever is under the crosshair: Smite for the undead, Bane of Arthropods for spiders, Sharpness for the rest.
survivalkit.setting.autoweapon.source.to: What the weapon in hand is picked by. A mob under the crosshair always comes first. With the second option and nothing aimed at, the hostile mobs in range are counted by their best weapon and the majority's weapon is taken in hand; on a tie the nearest mob decides. A new majority has to last at least a second before the weapon changes.
survivalkit.setting.autoweapon.range.too: How many blocks away hostile mobs still count, for the majority and for the ready slot. Mobs that are not hostile, like cows and villagers, and players never count.
survivalkit.setting.autoweapon.types.too: Which weapons may be taken out. An axe hits harder but recovers slower; swords only by default.
survivalkit.setting.autoweapon.durabilit: A weapon with fewer uses left than this is never taken out, so it does not break mid-fight. 0 lets weapons be used to the last use.
survivalkit.setting.autoweapon.targets.t: Who a weapon is picked for. Mobs only by default; other players only when you choose so.
survivalkit.setting.autoweapon.auto_atta: Hit what the crosshair is on as soon as the attack cooldown is full, never before. Only what you aim at; nothing is aimed for you.
survivalkit.setting.autoweapon.prep_slot: Hotbar slot (1-9) where the best weapon for the majority of hostile mobs around is put before you aim, from anywhere in the inventory. 0 is off. What you hold is never changed by it.
survivalkit.setting.autoweapon.select_pr: Also take the readied slot in hand. Off by default: the weapon waits in its slot and your hand stays as it is.
survivalkit.setting.autoweapon.lock_seco: For this long after you hit something or take a hit, no weapon change is made that would reset the attack cooldown. Switching between two of the same item (say, two iron swords) does not reset it, so that is allowed, and so is any switch once the cooldown is already full. 0 is off.
survivalkit.setting.autoweapon.lock_aim: Hold the weapon on aim too
The lock also holds back the switch on aim and the switch for the majority around. Off, the best weapon always comes out on aim, even if that resets the cooldown.
survivalkit.module.toolpicker.desc: Middle-click a block to take the best tool for it. Uses Auto Tool's block lists and durability threshold.
survivalkit.setting.toolpicker.mode.tool: What a middle click on a block does. Always a tool never picks the block itself; the second option picks the block when you carry it and the tool when you do not; off leaves the game's pick block as it is. In creative the game's pick block always runs.
survivalkit.setting.toolpicker.scope.too: Where tools may be found. With the whole inventory, a tool from the backpack is swapped into the slot in hand.
survivalkit.module.autotool.desc: Takes out the best tool when you start breaking a block, and puts back what you held once you stop.
survivalkit.setting.autotool.durability_: A tool with fewer uses left than this is never taken out, so it does not break in your hand. 0 lets tools be used to the last use.
While you hold a sword, hitting a block does not swap it for a tool — a fight is not disarmed by a stray click.
survivalkit.setting.autotool.keep_silk_t: A Silk Touch tool in hand stays on the blocks it is the tool for — a pickaxe on stone, a shovel on grass — so you get the block itself. On other blocks the right tool still comes out.
survivalkit.setting.autotool.only_with_t: Only with a tool in hand
Switch only when you already hold a pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe or shears. With bare hands, food or a block in hand, hitting a block leaves your hand as it is.
survivalkit.setting.autotool.silk_touch_: For these blocks a Silk Touch tool is taken even if a faster one is in reach. It still has to be able to drop the block.
survivalkit.setting.autotool.fortune_blo: For these blocks the tool with the highest Fortune is taken even if a faster one is in reach. It still has to be able to drop the block.
survivalkit.setting.autotool.scope.toolt: Where tools may be found. With the whole inventory, a tool from the backpack is swapped into the slot in hand and swapped back afterwards.
survivalkit.setting.autotool.restore_pre: Put back what you held once you let go of attack, or after a second of hitting nothing. A run of blocks is one switch out and one back. Off means the tool stays in hand.
survivalkit.module.veinminer.desc: Breaks a whole tree or ore vein at once through the server's own commands (/loot, /give, /fill, /setblock — whichever you may run). Does nothing on a server that does not give you /setblock.
survivalkit.setting.veinminer.trigger_ke: The key that sets it off while the module is on. Unbound by default: nothing happens until you pick one.
survivalkit.setting.veinminer.mode.toolt: Hold and break: hold the key and break a log or ore the usual way, the rest of the tree or vein follows. Look and press: look at it and press the key once; press again to stop halfway.
survivalkit.setting.veinminer.show_outli: Draws a frame round every block that would go: while the key is held in hold-and-break mode, whenever you look at a block in look-and-press mode. No frame means nothing would go — not in the list, not a natural tree, or no /setblock.
survivalkit.setting.veinminer.blocks.too: What a tree or vein may be made of. Only blocks of the same kind as the one you start from are followed; an ore and its deepslate version count as one kind.
survivalkit.setting.veinminer.max_blocks: No more blocks than this go at once, nearest first, counting the one you start from.
survivalkit.setting.veinminer.natural_tr: Logs are only broken when leaves the world grew touch them, so a log house next to a tree is left alone. Placed leaves do not count. A house that touches the tree itself is part of the same pile and would go with it.
survivalkit.setting.veinminer.drops.tool: Where the drops go when the server lets you run /loot; then Fortune and Silk Touch on your main hand count. Without /loot: with Silk Touch the blocks themselves come with /give; with Fortune on an ore the drops are rolled by vanilla's own rules and come with /give, the XP with /xp if you may run it; otherwise they drop where they stood as if broken by hand, with ore XP. Known gaps: the tool loses no durability, /loot gives no XP, and what does not fit in the inventory is lost.
survivalkit.setting.veinminer.commands_p: Never more than this many commands in any one second, spread out evenly, so the server does not take them for spam.
survivalkit.setting.veinminer.hide_feedb: While a tree or vein is being broken, the server's replies to these commands ("Changed the block", "Dropped items", "Gave items") stay out of your chat. Other operators may still see them.
survivalkit.veinminer.no_permission: Vein Breaker: you do not have /setblock on this server, so nothing was broken.
survivalkit.veinminer.no_effect_permissi: Vein Breaker: you do not have /effect on this server to pay the hunger cost, so nothing was broken. With the cost at 0 it works without.
survivalkit.veinminer.too_hungry: Vein Breaker: this job costs %s hunger points and your hunger bar cannot spare them, so nothing was broken.
survivalkit.veinminer.outside_area: Vein Breaker: nothing to break inside the Build Mode area.
survivalkit.veinminer.no_area: Vein Breaker: no Build Mode area, and it is set not to work without one.
survivalkit.setting.veinminer.without_ar: What to do when no Build Mode area is in force: Build Mode is off, or no area is marked in this dimension. With an area in force only the blocks inside it go; the part of the tree or vein outside it stays as it is.
survivalkit.setting.veinminer.blocks_per: One hunger point (half a drumstick) for every this many blocks broken; blocks left over count towards the next job. 0 is free. Paid with a short Hunger effect through the server's /effect, saturation first; without /effect Vein Breaker does nothing. A job that would take your hunger bar below 7, where you can no longer sprint, does not start. On Peaceful the hunger bar does not drop, so there the cost only takes saturation.
The tool in your main hand wears as if you had broken every block with it by hand: its damage per block for each one (1 for a pickaxe or axe, 2 for a sword), and Unbreaking spares some of it the way the game does. Set with the server's /item; without /item, Vein Breaker does nothing while you hold a tool that wears. The tool never breaks: a job that would leave it with nothing does not start. Unbreakable items and items that are not tools do not wear.
survivalkit.veinminer.no_item_permission: Vein Breaker: you do not have /item on this server to wear the tool, so nothing was broken. With tool wear off it works without.
survivalkit.veinminer.tool_too_worn: Vein Breaker: this job would take %s durability from your tool and it has %s left; it must not break, so nothing was broken.
survivalkit.module.buildmode.desc: Marks an area with a wand and keeps the block-breaking modules inside it. The area is drawn in the world and kept per server and dimension. /bolge shows it (goster), clears it (temizle), or puts a corner where you stand (kose1, kose2).
survivalkit.setting.buildmode.wand.toolt: The items that mark the corners while the module is on: in hand, a left click on a block marks the first corner and a right click the second, and neither breaks nor places anything. Auto Weapon and Auto Tool leave the wand where it is. With the module off it is an ordinary item.
survivalkit.buildmode.no_area: Build Mode: no area is marked in this dimension.
survivalkit.buildmode.cleared: Build Mode: the area in this dimension was cleared.
survivalkit.buildmode.off: Build Mode is off: the area is kept but holds nothing back for now.
survivalkit.buildmode.not_in_world: Build Mode: you are not in a world.
survivalkit.module.wdl.desc: Writes the chunks you walk through on a server to disk; open them in singleplayer afterwards.
survivalkit.wdl.forbidden: This server does not allow downloading the world, so nothing is being saved.
survivalkit.setting.wdl.continue_world: Keep adding to the same world
survivalkit.setting.wdl.continue_world.t: Every download from the same server goes into one world, named after its address. Chunks seen again are updated; the ones not seen this time stay as they were, and chests opened before keep their contents. Off starts a new world, stamped with the date, each time.
survivalkit.setting.wdl.seed.tooltip: Paste it here if the server answers /seed; left empty, 0 is written.
Ask the server for /seed automatically on connect if the player has permission, and write the answer to the seed setting.
survivalkit.setting.wdl.ownership.toolti: How to handle ownership of tamed entities (dogs, cats, horses, etc.) when saving: As is keeps existing owners, Transfer to me makes them yours.
survivalkit.setting.wdl.flush_interval.t: How often loaded chunks are saved and flushed to disk, in seconds.
survivalkit.setting.wdl.save_player_stat: Start with own inventory and position
When opening the downloaded world in singleplayer, start with your inventory, equipment, position, XP, and health from the server; if disabled, standard world spawn is used.
survivalkit.wdl.command.status.active: World download is active: %s chunks saved -> %s
survivalkit.wdl.command.saved: World download saved (%s chunks flushed to disk).
survivalkit.wdl.command.not_in_world: Cannot download world: not connected to any world.
survivalkit.module.scaffold.desc: Puts a block under your next step when there is nothing there, so you can walk out over a gap. Your view is never turned: the block goes down with the same click you would make on the block beside it.
survivalkit.module.hud.desc: Boxes of information on the screen: which modules are on, and what they have to say. Hidden with F1 and while the debug screen is up.
survivalkit.setting.hud.shown.tooltip: Whether this box is on the screen at all. Off, it is not drawn; the rest of the HUD stays.
survivalkit.setting.hud.anchor.tooltip: Which corner or edge of the screen the box is measured from. It keeps its distance from there whatever size the window is.
survivalkit.setting.hud.offset_x.tooltip: How far in from the corner's side edge the box is, in screen units. From a middle, how far right of centre; negative is left.
survivalkit.setting.hud.offset_y.tooltip: How far in from the top or bottom edge the box is, in screen units.
survivalkit.setting.hud.scale.tooltip: How big the box is: 100 is the game's own text size, 50 half, 300 three times.
survivalkit.setting.hud.active_sort.tool: How the modules that are on are listed: by name, longest name first, or as the menu lists them.
survivalkit.setting.hud.active_sort.name: By name
survivalkit.hud.wdl_refused: World Downloader: the server does not allow it
survivalkit.hud.editor.title: HUD editor
survivalkit.hud.editor.hint: Drag a box to move it · right click puts it back
survivalkit.menu.profile.taken: There is one by that name
survivalkit.menu.preset.taken: There is a preset by that name
survivalkit.menu.preset.undo: Back to what it was before the preset
survivalkit.rules.title: Profile by server
survivalkit.rules.list: Address rules — top to bottom, the first that matches wins
survivalkit.rules.hint: * matches anything: *.example.net matches example.net and every address under it. The port counts only if you write one.
survivalkit.setting.common.action_bar: Show on the action bar too
survivalkit.setting.common.action_bar.to: What this module says on the HUD is also said above the hotbar, where the game puts its own short messages. Off, it is on the HUD only.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.delay.toolt: Ticks to wait after putting blocks down before the next ones. 0 places every tick; 20 is a second.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.per_tick.to: The most blocks put down in one tick. 1 is enough for walking; more helps when sprinting or reaching ahead.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.fill_air.to: Put a block where there is air under the next step — or grass, snow and other things a block simply replaces.
Put a block where there is water under the next step, so you walk over it instead of swimming.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.fill_lava.t: Put a block where there is lava under the next step, so you walk over it instead of into it.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.support_mod: Which blocks a new bridge may start from. With "Only listed blocks" it starts only against a listed block, then goes on along the blocks Scaffold put down itself.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.supports.to: With "Only listed blocks", the blocks a bridge may start from. Empty, any block will do. Ignored with "Any block".
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.preferred.t: Built with in this order: the first one you carry is used. Drag to reorder. When none is in reach, the fallback decides.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.blocked.too: Never put down, even when listed above. Sand and gravel fall, TNT is TNT, and a chest or shulker box put down is everything in it gone from your inventory.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.prefer_full: Between stacks of the same block, a full stack is used before a partly used one.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.fallback.to: What to build with when nothing from "Blocks to use" is in reach. Only whole blocks you can stand on are ever used, never slabs or torches.
If you carry the block you are standing on, build with it first; otherwise "Blocks to use" decides. "Never use" still holds.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.torches.too: Every so many blocks of bridge, hang a torch from your inventory on the bridge's side, below the walkway, so it never blocks your way. With no room for it there, it goes beside the next block instead. Out of torches, you are told once.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.torch_inter: How many blocks of bridge between two torches.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.scope.toolt: Where blocks may be found. With the whole inventory, a stack from the backpack is swapped into the slot in hand and swapped back afterwards.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.restore_pre: Put back what you held half a second after the last block went down. Off means the blocks stay in hand.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.extend.tool: While walking, also fill this many blocks straight on past the next step, so the bridge is ahead of you. 0 fills only the next step.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.keep_y.tool: A bridge stays on the level it started on until it is finished, even if you step up onto something on the way. Jumping never lifts the bridge either way; only the tower does.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.y_lock.tool: While on, every block goes in the same Y: jumping, or jumping while running, it still goes there rather than under you, and the bridge stays flat. Placed as long as you can reach it. No tower while on. "Where I started": the block under your feet when you switched Scaffold on.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.fixed_y.too: The Y the blocks go in while the Y lock is on "Set Y": the bridge itself is at this height, and you walk on top of it.
Press it and the locked Y moves to where you are: the block under your feet. On "Set Y" the number changes too. Unbound by default.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.tower.toolt: When you jump straight up, a block goes under your feet once you are a block higher, and you land on it. Only the game's own jump: nothing makes you rise faster.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.tower_only_: Build the tower only while the jump key is held down. Off, any jump puts a block under you.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.descend.too: With the Y lock on, every press of sneak takes the locked Y a block down and the bridge carries on a step lower. Only your own key counts, never the sneak of "Stop at edges": that still stops you at a real edge, but lets you walk down the step.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.ramp.toolti: For every block you go on, the bridge goes a block higher (Up) or lower (Down), along the way you first walk. With the Y lock on, the lock slides along with it. Going up you have to jump at every step: a step is a whole block, which cannot be walked up. Every step takes two blocks, the step and the one under it. No tower while on.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.width.toolt: How many blocks wide the bridge is. 3 reaches a block out on both sides of you, 2 on the side you are nearer. Every extra block is another block from your inventory.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.diagonal.to: Walking slantwise, also fill the corner between two blocks that would otherwise meet only at an edge. Without it such a block has no face to be put against, and the bridge stops there.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.safe_walk.t: SafeWalk: holds the game's own sneak, which keeps you from walking off an edge. At an edge: only when there is nothing yet under the step you are heading for — out of blocks, outside the area, a gap left alone. Always: the whole time Scaffold is on.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.pause_with_: Put nothing down while the inventory, chat or any other screen is open.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.pause_while: Put nothing down while falling further than a jump: a block caught on the way down is not what a fall is for.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.pause_in_la: Put nothing down while you are in lava.
survivalkit.scaffold.no_support: Scaffold: no listed block to build against
survivalkit.scaffold.supports_empty: List empty: builds against any block
Show in Scaffold's HUD box how many blocks you have left to build with, and say so when there are none. With "Show on the action bar too" on, above the hotbar as well.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.low_warning: With fewer blocks than this left, the count turns into a warning. 0 never warns.
survivalkit.setting.scaffold.show_target: Draw a green box where the next block will go, so you see it before it is there — or see where one is missing.
